Rezolve AI Ramps Up Dealmaking as E-Commerce Turns to AI — Interview
By Connor Hart
Customers aren't arriving at e-commerce sites through search engines anymore, according to Rezolve AI Chief Executive Daniel Wagner.
Rather, shoppers are increasingly turning to artificial intelligence for product recommendations and connections to trusted retailers.

"It's a completely new way of interacting using generative AI," Wagner said in an interview Tuesday. "Most of these retailers and brands have no clue and are really frightened of this new world, because they don't know how to approach it."
That is where Rezolve comes in. The company is helping retailers navigate the shift, having spent much of the past decade building out an infrastructure platform that powers agentic commerce.
Now, the investments are beginning to pay off, Wagner said.
Rezolve's customer base stood at over 1,640 as of June 30, up from about 950 at the end of 2025. Deals are being completed on accelerated timelines, and the momentum is palpable, Wagner said.
"Just the other week, we met with a customer on a Monday, and they signed on a Thursday," he said, adding that B2B deals typically operate on much longer cycles.

The influx in customers led to a surge in revenue. Revenue jumped to $130.8 million during the first half of 2026, up from $6.3 million a year earlier. Over the same period, Rezolve widened its loss to $139.5 million from $57.9 million.
Shares fell 9.3%, to $2.62, shortly ahead of Tuesday's opening bell.

The company noted that its revenue is seasonally weighted toward the back half of the year, with peak retail and holiday trading, enterprise deployment timing and increasing partner-led distribution expected to produce a materially stronger second half.
Rezolve said it continues to expect revenue of about $360 million for the year.

Looking ahead, Wagner said the company can further expedite its growth by licensing its infrastructure. Proof-of-concept came last week, when Google chose to deploy Rezolve's proprietary distributed database technology within Google Cloud.

The selection represented the first major commercial deployment of Rezolve's distributed database platform by one of the world's leading technology companies, and it bodes well for continued adoption.

"We are selling our products into a broad base of customers in multiple verticals, and now, we are seeing large, respected tech companies licensing our core infrastructure to do their own thing," Wagner said.
"I think we are showing that we are one of the key players in this new world," he concluded.
